title: Buttons in dataframe / table cells with callbacks
body: ### Summary Allow adding action buttons to dataframe rows, which can be configured to trigger an action in the Streamlit app for a specific row. ### How? Could be implemented via column config (`st.columnConfig.ButtonColumn`) or as a new parameter that can be configured with `st.dataframe`, e.g.: `st.dataframe(..., actions=[])`. ### Additional Context Inspirations: Related to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10212

comments.body:
Hey [USER],

Thanks for sharing this request! 

Displaying a table with a link in a cell is already possible today via `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor` (check out the doc [here](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/data/st.column_config/st.column_config.linkcolumn)). Using this functionality, you could add a link to a specific page to your `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor.`

What's not possible today is displaying a button within a cell of `st.dataframe` or `st.data_editor` or programmatically switching navigating the pages of your app.

There is an open feature request **[here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4832)** for programmatically navigating the pages of your multipage app – please upvote that request if you'd like to see it prioritized.

I'd like to +1 this feature request as well. There are [many widgets](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.column_config) that can be used with `st.dataframe`, yet a **button** or **internal link** are missing.

My use case would be a list of items where each item can have some related operations: view details, edit entry (via dialog), delete entry, go to a different page related to this entry... This is basically a button or link with a callback.

Although, there may be limitations to implementing a callback function to a link/button in a dataframe cell, it would be a very useful feature that I've seen requested many times when researching this topic.

The current way to solve it is to create [`st.columns`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/layout/st.columns) and populating the cells with said buttons/links. That is a workaround, more cumbersome to code and, although looks OK (IMHO) it _feels_ wrong when it would be more appropriate to use [`st.dataframe`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe) or [`st.table`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.table), especially considering all the [nice column configurations we already get](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.column_config).
Agree on all what's been said so far, and my use-case is also very similar to [USER]'s. I've been wanting to use buttons in tables multiple times now.
